<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-indent:-18.0pt;line-height:15.0pt;
mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><!--[if !supportLists]--><span style="font-size:10.5pt;
font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;,sans-serif;mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;;
mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">1.<span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span><!--[endif]--><span style="font-size:10.5pt;font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;,sans-serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">The proposed rear dormer roof
extension, by reason of its scale, siting and excessive bulk, would result in an
overly dominant addition covering a substantial portion of the roof slope failing
to remain subordinate to the host dwelling. The proposal would therefore harm
the character of the roofscape and fail to preserve or enhance the character
and appearance of the John Innes Merton Park Conservation Area, resulting in
less than substantial harm for which no public benefit has been identified. The
proposal is contrary to Sections 66 and 72 of the Planning (Listed Buildings
and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Chapter 16 of the NPPF, Policy HC1 of the
London Plan, and Policies D12.1, D12.2, D12.3, D12.4 and D12.5 of the Merton
Local Plan 2024.<o:p></o:p></span></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-indent:-18.0pt;line-height:15.0pt;
mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><!--[if !supportLists]--><span style="font-size:10.5pt;
font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;,sans-serif;mso-fareast-font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;;
mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">1.<span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </span></span><!--[endif]--><span style="font-size:10.5pt;font-family:&quot;Segoe UI&quot;,sans-serif;mso-fareast-font-family:
&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-fareast-language:EN-GB">The proposed insertion of five
side windows, by reason of their quantum, siting and poor arrangement, would
appear excessive and fail to reflect the established fenestration pattern of
the host dwelling. This would result in visual clutter and harm to the
architectural character of the building, failing to preserve or enhance the
character and appearance of the John Innes Merton Park Conservation Area,
resulting in less than substantial harm for which no public benefit has been
identified. The proposal is contrary to Sections 66 and 72 of the Planning
(Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas) Act 1990, Chapter 16 of the NPPF,
Policy HC1 of the London Plan, and Policies D12.1, D12.2, D12.3, D12.4 and
D12.5 of the Merton Local Plan 2024.<o:p></o:p></span></p>

<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="text-indent:-18.0pt;mso-list:l0 level1 lfo1"><!--[if !supportLists]-->1.<span style="font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; font-size-adjust: none; font-language-override: normal; font-kerning: auto; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-feature-settings: normal; font-variation-settings: normal; font-stretch: normal; font-size: 7pt; line-height: normal; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</span><!--[endif]-->In the absence of an Arboricultural Survey,
Arboricultural Impact Assessment, Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree
Protection Plan, the proposal fails to demonstrate that the development would
not adversely impact the health and longevity of trees within and adjacent to
the site, including the Tree Preservation Order holly tree to the front. The
Local Planning Authority cannot therefore be satisfied that important landscape
features, which contribute positively to the character and appearance of the
Conservation Area, would be adequately protected during construction. The
proposal is therefore contrary to London Plan Policy G7 and Merton Local Plan
2024 Policy O15.4.<o:p></o:p></p>
